source.title: On the robustness of noisy solutions in non-convex neural networks
source.authors: E. M. Malatesta; A. Passalacqua; Riccardo Zecchina

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The study analytically examines finite-temperature training-error configurations and numerically tests a message-passing search for them in binary perceptrons. This bears conceptually on training-error outcomes, but uses a different model and method from the versions' neural-network benchmark settings.
record.gate_note: The study tests binary perceptrons with Ising weights, not large convolutional networks, CIFAR benchmarks, random initialization of neural networks, or the initialization, normalization, shortcut, and learning-rate conditions in the versions. Its results concern training errors, OGP thresholds, and algorithmic accessibility; only results that directly report training-error outcomes are included as rows. Cited prior-work results are not extracted as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study investigates discrete binary perceptrons using replica analysis and reinforced approximate message passing. Its training-error results do not test V1's convolutional networks trained with SGD or Adam, or any other version's specified mechanisms. Binary teacher–student geometry also does not test V2's two-layer ReLU gradient-descent claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that error-counting equilibrium measures remain frozen at finite temperature, while atypical dense finite-error regions persist beyond the zero-temperature OGP threshold and can be reached by rAMP with useful generalization. The OGP threshold estimates use an RS approximation with an acknowledged non-physical clone-count dependence.
record.recipe_differences: Finite-temperature Gibbs weighting and reinforced approximate message passing for binary perceptrons, rather than gradient-based SGD or Adam training of convolutional networks from random initialization. The analysis also uses replica calculations and OGP geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: Target training error, inverse temperature β, reinforcement rate ρ, constraint density α, and temperature annealing (which the authors report gave no substantial improvement).

fits_no_version.finding: Allowing positive training error shifts rAMP's empirical success transition to larger constraint densities in storage-setting binary perceptrons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Finite-temperature reinforced message passing can find low-error binary-perceptron assignments at densities where its exact-fit search fails.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed reinforcement rate, only β = 4 among tested temperatures reaches 0.025 training error within 10^4 iterations; β = ∞ produces diverging updates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Binary-perceptron rAMP performance depends on inverse temperature and its interaction with reinforcement.

fits_no_version.finding: Error-counting Gibbs weights retain a frozen solution at every finite temperature. The boundary-smoothness analysis gives conditions under which freezing disappears.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Freezing in binary-perceptron equilibrium measures depends on the boundary behavior of the single-pattern Gibbs weight.

fits_no_version.finding: Replica calculations predict increasing finite-error OGP thresholds, but their non-monotonic dependence on clone count is explicitly identified as an RS artifact.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Permitting training errors relaxes binary-perceptron overlap-gap obstructions, subject to limitations of the replica-symmetric threshold estimates.

fits_no_version.finding: Teacher–student calculations and rAMP experiments indicate accessible finite-error dense regions with favorable generalization beyond the zero-temperature OGP threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Finite-error dense regions can preserve useful generalization while extending algorithmic accessibility in binary teacher–student perceptrons.

record.peer_reviewed: Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment
record.problems: Algorithmic success probabilities are shown in figures without exact values in the prose; results average over 60 samples in Figure 4, but no uncertainty intervals are stated. The OGP calculations use an RS Ansatz for the cloned system, and the authors explicitly call its non-monotonic threshold behavior non-physical and say the resulting threshold is an upper bound to the appearance of an overlap-gapped phase.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Replica calculations of OGP thresholds and generalization-error curves do not directly report the training-error behavior named by V1; cited thresholds and prior-work results are not extracted as current-study training outcomes.

untested.parts: All: convolutional-network training error under SGD or Adam on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random labels and model-size or regularization conditions.
All: spurious minima under gradient descent in two-layer ReLU teacher–student networks and the effect of extra student neurons.
All: training degradation with convolutional depth, identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization exceptions.
All: activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, learning speed, and trainable depth.
All: learning-rate stability thresholds, curvature dynamics, recovery, and divergence during gradient training.
All: batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Different architecture and optimization method do not by themselves establish a scope limitation of V1. None of the supplied versions is tested, so the record's V1 limits_scope verdict should be removed.

versions.untested_parts: Tests binary perceptrons with Gaussian patterns and random labels in storage, not convolutional networks, SGD or Adam, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels on those benchmarks, or smaller network sizes and regularized recipes.

rows.subject: rAMP
rows.operation_detail: Runs fixed-temperature reinforced AMP on storage-setting ABP datasets and measures the probability of finding a configuration under the target training-error threshold.

conditions.value: β = ∞; procedure reduces to standard zero temperature rAMP

rows.measure: Empirical success probability of finding a configuration at or below the target training error as a function of constraint density α.
rows.uncertainty: 60 samples; sigmoid fits shown, but no uncertainty interval stated.
rows.locator: Figure 4, left panel; Sec. IV A
rows.note: The text says allowing larger training error shifts the algorithmic transition to larger constraint densities. The figure plots success probability against α for several targets; it does not give textual numeric success probabilities.
rows.check: The zero-error success curve concerns binary-perceptron rAMP, outside V1's system and optimizer. A curve across constraint densities cannot receive a single partial state for V1.

rows.subject: rAMP
rows.operation_detail: Runs rAMP on a storage-setting ABP dataset at fixed reinforcement rate and compares training-error trajectories across inverse temperatures.

conditions.value: same dataset and initialization across curves

rows.measure: Training error along the rAMP trajectory; whether it reaches ϵtarg = 0.025.
rows.baseline: Other tested β trajectories; only β = 4 reaches the target.
rows.value: Only β = 4 reaches the target within 104 iterations.
rows.note: The text states only one of the values considered reaches the stated target; the figure gives the trajectories, but other exact end errors are not stated.
rows.check: Reaching the target at β = 4 is correctly reported, but binary-perceptron message passing does not measure V1. The iteration limit is 10^4.

rows.subject: rAMP
rows.operation_detail: Runs rAMP on a storage-setting ABP dataset with β = ∞; trajectory is reported to stop before the iteration limit because updates diverge.

conditions.value: same dataset and initialization as other Figure 11 curves

rows.value: Trajectory stops before reaching the maximum number of iterations because rAMP produces diverging updates.
rows.note: The authors relate the difficulty to α > 0.784 and note that solutions do not exist above αS = 0.833 in the large-N limit; these are contextual thresholds, not additional per-run measurements.
rows.check: Diverging rAMP updates are correctly reported but test neither V1 nor V5. β is inverse temperature, not a gradient-descent learning rate; α = 0.9 also exceeds the cited asymptotic storage satisfiability threshold.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The study reports that allowing positive training error shifts the algorithmic transition to larger α, while the exact-fit run and some tested temperatures do not reach the target under the reported setup (R1–R8). This is a different model and algorithm from V1's neural-network benchmark claim.
